Headteacher's Welcome
A very warm welcome to the Hamp Academy website.
We are extremely proud of our caring and supportive school community where we celebrate and develop the wide and varied skills and interests of our children through a broad and balanced curriculum.
Our intention is to provide high quality teaching with high expectations that encourages the children to grow into confident and happy learners and individuals who are able to fulfil their potential and achieve their best. Above all we want our children to become well-rounded individuals who have a healthy respect for both themselves and those around them.
We hope the website gives you a feel for what we are about and provides you with the information you need. Prospective parents are most welcome to visit the school and meet the staff and children; we look forward to working with you to help your child grow and flourish.
Miss S A Hitchings

Free School meals
Children who attend a Somerset school, whose parents or carers receive certain benefits, may be entitled to free school meals.
Children eligible for free school meals must be in school all day. They will be provided with a meal at lunchtime which is paid for by the school.
Parents or carers are responsible for registering their entitlement and requesting free school meals for their children.
Parents and carers who receive any of the following are entitled to free school meals:
Only the benefits listed above qualify for free school meals. If you have recently become unemployed, but are still receiving Working Tax Credits, you may be entitled to free school meals. Please phone us on 0300 123 2224 for advice.
If you meet the criteria listed above, please complete the application form online.

If this applies to you, please complete the Free School Meals to Families with No Recourse to Public Funds form (PDF) and return it with the appropriate evidence to fsm@somerset.gov.uk.
To apply for Free School Meals and to see if you are eligible, please visit:
https://www.gov.uk/apply-free-school-meals
Enter your postcode, this will take you to Somerset County Council website.
Click on the Apply Now button at the bottom of the page.
Somerset County Council will check your eligibility and let you know the outcome of your application, usually within 10 working days.
If your child is starting in September, you should apply during the summer holidays. Applying too early could result in your application being removed.

Friends of Hamp
We are very fortunate at our school to have a Hamp Friends of School Association that is and has been such an integral part of the school for several years.
In its times the Association has raised thousands of pounds, which have been spent on improving equipment and resources to enhance our children’s education and the facilities in the school.
We run a variety of activities through the year such as discos, School Tuck Shop at breaktimes and family events. Over the years the money raised has purchased computers, cameras and other equipment which are used regularly by our children!
As we have only a small group of regular people attending – volunteering at events we are always in need of anyone new who can assist. If you feel you can volunteer your time please let us know.
We meet at the school (time and dates to be arranged) for our meetings . The purpose of the meetings is to think of lots of fantastic ideas for new events and money raising opportunities in a very informal friendly environment! It’s a fantastic way to meet new people and other parents.
How do I get involved? Just email us on office@hampacademy.co.uk

Parents Evenings
Parent Consultations
At Hamp Academy, we understand the importance of regular communication between parents, teachers, and pupils. This is why we schedule parent consultations throughout the year.
Scheduling Consultations
We hold parent consultations at the end of Autumn 1 and Spring 2. These are valuable opportunities for you to discuss your child's progress with their teacher.
Booking Appointments
Appointments for parent consultations can be booked via the Arbor App. This online platform allows you to easily schedule a consultation at a time that suits you.
We encourage all parents to take advantage of this opportunity to discuss their child's progress and work together to support their academic and personal development.

Uniform
Requirements for School Uniform
The School uniform should be worn by all pupils throughout the school day, on the way to and from school and when representing the School. We expect all pupils to take pride in their appearance and to remember at all times that they are ambassadors for their school.
In order to keep school uniform costs to a minimum please note that items with a school logo are entirely optional
We have a selection of second-hand school uniform available. Please ask at the school office if you would like to find out more. We also warmly welcome donations of good-quality uniform that your child has outgrown.

School uniform is stocked throughout the year so is always available for parents to buy Monday to Saturday 9-5 in store or 24-7 from our e-commerce website www.swschoolwear.co.uk from 14 th November 2022.
We are pleased to supply 120 schools in the area, we have onsite production of embroidery and printing which enables us to ensure consistency of supply with a time managed turnaround and stock availability all year round including specialist sizes to order.

Curriculum Overview
At Hamp Academy, we have designed our curriculum, so as to place a high priority on improving the basic knowledge within all subjects, especially in the core subjects of English, maths, science and ICT.
It is our aim to provide an exciting and stimulating curriculum that provides as many opportunities as possible for our children to achieve and become well-rounded individuals. When appropriate our curriculum is tailored for the individual needs of children, including social and emotional support and specific SEN plans.
Our curriculum encourages all pupils to understand, be interested in and show respect to others and their beliefs, whilst also developing their own self-esteem and knowledge of their place in the wider world, e-safety and of British Values. The values of SMSC are of great importance to us and underpin our curriculum approach.
Skills, Knowledge and Understanding
To ensure that we teach a broad and balanced curriculum, we follow the New National Curriculum programmes of study (September 2014), covering the key knowledge required in all KS2 subjects. With understanding, we can then focus on skills. Learning the skills for individual subjects, such as reading co-ordinates on maps in geography and analysing primary and secondary sources in history, is central to the teaching of individual lessons within our curriculum. For the whole school curriculum topic map, calculation policies and English policies, please see the subsequent dropdowns. To find out further details of the curriculum content in the different year groups, please see the relevant pages.
Extra-Curricular Opportunities
Central to the life in our school are the many extra-curricular and enrichment opportunities that we provide for our children. A particular strength is the after-school clubs that run every afternoon until 4pm, ranging from choir and dance club to times tables and art club.
What does your child learn at school each day? Find information about our curriculum subjects here.

SEND
Hamp Academy is an inclusive, mainstream junior school for children in Years 3 to Year 6 (Key Stage 2). Here at Hamp Academy the individual child is at the heart of all we do.
All staff at Hamp Academy are committed to nurturing the whole child and work as hard to support the child’s emotional and social wellbeing as we do the academic progress.
All staff at Hamp Academy are aware of the need for trauma informed practices and have a sound understanding of attachment issues in young children.
Our staff are also trained in Restorative Practice.
We aim to ensure that: Staff have high aspirations for every child, celebrating individual differences in ability, aptitude, emotional development, behaviour and skills. We endeavour to meet all individual need, providing opportunities for all students to reach their full potential. Students with learning difficulties are able to access their entitlement to a broad, balanced and relevant curriculum as part of the whole school community.
We identify and assess children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEN) as early and as thoroughly as possible using the revised Code of Practice (2015).
We maintain up-to-date knowledge of current SEN good practice and methodology in order to offer support and training in these areas to all staff in the school.
Our SEN provision aims to fulfil the expectations of the Core Standards – Somerset’s published expectations for all settings regarding the provision of SEN.
The Somerset SEN local offer is accessible at: www.somerset.gov.uk.
